title: TE Jack Eubanks et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Items 2 and 3 were sustained; Items 1, 4, and 5 were not sustained. No express remedial order was stated.
first_summary: Complainants challenged the legality of Presbytery’s called meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adopted adjudication sustained the objections to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote and ordering it to reassemble and revote. It rejected the challenges to the called meeting, Presbytery’s involvement in membership, and its consideration of David Alexander’s complaint. No express remedy was ordered.
summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery’s called meeting and its actions concerning a judicial commission and church membership. The adopted adjudication sustained the objection to dissolving the commission by a 14–12 vote because Robert’s Rules required a two-thirds vote, and sustained without stated grounds the objection to ordering the dissolved commission to reassemble and revote. It rejected the challenges to the called meeting, Presbytery’s membership action, and its consideration of David Alexander’s complaint; the membership claim failed because church membership is not itself a court. No express remedy was ordered.
